text:
Two men are drinking in a bar
They pull out the sandwiches their wives had lovingly prepared and tuck in.
The bartender comes over and says "you can't eat your own food in here"
So they swapped sandwiches.
gist: Two men eating homemade sandwiches in a bar are told they cannot eat their own food, so they swap sandwiches.

characters.looks: two working men, flat caps, beer mugs

text:
A 7-year-old is sitting on a park bench eating a chocolate bar.
The man sitting next to him looks over and says, "Eating that many chocolate bars is bad for you."
The boy looks over and responds, "My great grandfather lived to be one hundred and five".
The man replies, "And he ate that much chocolate?"
"No" says the boy, "But he minded his own fucking business."
gist: Stranger lectures a boy about eating chocolate; the boy cites his long-lived great-grandfather, whose secret was minding his own business.

characters.looks: seven-year-old boy, pile of chocolate bars

text:
The penguin joke (my favorite joke)
One day a Cop pulls a van over and when he walks up to the window he sees ten penguins in the back.
The cop asks the man "are those your penguins?"
The man Says "yes, they are my pets."
The cop replies to the man "You need to take them to the zoo right now."
So the man agrees and drives off. The next day the cop pulls over the same van and he walks up to the window and sees the ten pengins all wearing sunglasses.
The cop says to the man "I thought i told you to take those penguins to the zoo."
The man says "I did, today we are going to the beach!"
gist: Cop orders a man with penguins in his van to take them to the zoo; next day the man explains they went to the zoo and are now going to the beach.

text:
My girlfriend's dog died, so to cheer her up I got her an identical one.
She was livid, "what am I going to do with two dead dogs?"
gist: Man replaces his girlfriend's dead dog with an identical one, but the replacement is also dead.

text:
Boy: What's a palindrome?
Teacher: racecar
{10 years later}
Boy: [bursting out of bank in ski mask] where's the palindrome
Getaway driver: [sitting in kayak]
gist: Boy learns 'racecar' as an example of a palindrome, and years later as a bank robber asks for 'the palindrome' getaway vehicle and gets a kayak.

wordplay.explanation: 'Racecar' and 'kayak' are both palindromes; the accomplice picked the wrong one.

characters.looks: schoolboy, later adult in ski mask
getaway driver in ski mask, sitting in kayak

text:
A boy scout says to his scout leader, "Sir, is this snake poisonous?" The scout leader says, "No, that snake's not poisonous at all." So the boy picks up the snake, which bites him and the boy starts to spasm and foam at the mouth as the other kids look on in horror...
The scout leader says, "But that snake is venomous. Poison is ingested or absorbed, while venom is injected. Let's get it right next time, boys."
gist: A scout leader says a snake is not poisonous, the boy is bitten and convulses, and the leader pedantically explains the snake is venomous, not poisonous.

characters.looks: boy scout in uniform and neckerchief
adult in scout uniform, hat, lecturing finger

adaptNote: Russian 'ядовитый' covers both; need another pedantic term pair

text:
A guy walks into a bar
A guy walks into a crowded local bar, holding a pistol in his hand and yelling, “I have a 45 caliber pistol here with seven rounds in the barrel plus one in the chamber and I want to know who’s been sleeping with my wife.”
A voice from the other end of the bar called out, “You’ll need more ammo”
gist: Armed husband demands to know who slept with his wife, and a voice in the bar says he will need more ammo, implying many men did.

characters.looks: furious man, red face, waving pistol, rumpled shirt
relaxed bar patron at far end, beer in hand
woman in flashy dress, seen in photo

text:
My neighbour knocked on my door at 2:30am this morning, can you believe that, 2:30am?!
Luckily for him I was still up playing my Bagpipes
gist: A man complains about his neighbor knocking at 2:30 a.m., then admits he was luckily still up playing the bagpipes, the obvious reason for the visit.

characters.looks: man in pajamas, holding bagpipes, indignant
